title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive identification failure at the front end of a policing deployment. An automated licence plate reader flagged a plate as stolen when it was not, and that single incorrect output became the factual basis for an armed traffic stop. The error was not caught before officers acted on it, and the stop escalated to a K-9 deployment, an arrest, and charges before anyone on scene confirmed the plate was clean.

The failure sits in the handoff between the camera system and the officers who receive its alerts. The system produced an identification, officers treated that identification as grounds for a stop, and no verification step stood between the two. Catching it would have required confirming the flagged plate against the vehicle actually in front of them, or a human review of the alert before it was dispatched as a reason to stop. The department's own K-9 policy lists factors handlers must weigh, which places a second decision point where the consequences of the first error could have been limited.

What is not established is why the camera misread the plate, whether the misread was a known limitation of the system, and what discipline or further action will follow for the officers under investigation. An internal investigation finding no wrongdoing is a departmental finding, not an adjudication of the underlying identification error.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop began after a FLOCK camera incorrectly flagged a license plate as stolen. The plate belonged to a Chevy Malibu, but the camera misread it on a red Dodge Ram. Officers stopped driver Brandon Upchurch with guns drawn and ordered him out. He raised his hands, asked why he was stopped, and was then arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. He received medical attention at the scene.

Officers later confirmed on camera that the plate was not stolen and called it a misread. Police said they believed Upchurch might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. The department's K-9 policy requires handlers to consider the crime's severity, threats to officers or citizens, and whether a suspect is resisting or fleeing. Multiple officers are under investigation, and the article does not say what discipline or further action may follow.
